name: postscript_interpreter
description: A PostScript interpreter, written in Rust, for watching PostScript programs draw live

paragraphs: pscat is a PostScript interpreter written in Rust. PostScript is a programming language for drawing pages; pscat runs your program and shows the picture as it is drawn, in a live window, or renders it to PNG, SVG or PDF. It also runs in a browser tab, and it ships with PostScript libraries for making art: generative patterns, paint and watercolor, printmaking, lettering, charts and more. It was built for fun, not as a Ghostscript replacement, though it aims for broad PostScript coverage over time.
jeromebanks.github.io/postscriptinterpreter has the docs, the full gallery, a specimen of every font, and a live playground that runs the interpreter in your browser, no install.

I used to write raw PostScript by hand in college and send it straight to a LaserWriter. This is a from-scratch Rust interpreter built to relive that — watching a hand-written recursive PostScript program draw itself, live, without depending on a decades-old C codebase to do it.
